_readme: CORRECTION SHEET for _jp1discs.json. Published BESIDE the frozen file, never into it:
COIN-JUDGE.md 1.1 — 'a corrected history entry sits next to the published one with both
values and the reason'. _jp1discs.json is hashed in _jp0hashes.json (roundTarget,
sha256 de72c3e35287a49d) and is left byte-identical so the penny round's numbers stay
reproducible. Read both through _jpdiscs.mjs, which merges them and refuses an entry
flagged unusable.
Two defects in the frozen file, ledger A15, both confirmed 2026-08-24:
1. penny-rev-1991d.png has NO entry at all, though it is a live reference.
2. penny-rev-artwork.jpg's entry is UNUSABLE and carries no flag. Its p95 residual is
13.93% of R with 244 of 720 rays terminating at the search-window end — a search
bound, not a fit (COIN-JUDGE 4.1). Every other entry in the file is p95 <= 2.13%,
and the two entries with a 3.4% / 5.2% A-vs-B disagreement DO carry a 'note'. The
single worst entry is the only silent one.
CONSEQUENCE, found while checking this: _jp15rev.mjs resolved discs as
`FROZEN[f] ?? FITTED[f]`, so its blend/grid/crop subcommands registered
penny-rev-artwork.jpg on the frozen R 252.41 / cy 222.30 instead of the good drawn-rim
fit R 174.89 / cy 262.62 that sits ten lines below in the same file — R 44.3% too large
and the centre 40.3 px off — while its own `discs` subcommand printed the good fit. That
precedence is corrected in _jp15rev.mjs; the frozen entry is untouched.
2026-08-24, ledger A28 — penny-rev.jpg is UNUSABLE FOR GEOMETRY. See `unusable` below.
It is NOT removed from T1's reverse pool: T1 needs a registration good enough for a
design NCC, not a viewBox coordinate, and it sorts penny-rev.jpg as a penny at 0.517
against 0.193 for the next denomination. A coordinate read off its disc is another
matter and is refused.

penny-rev-1991d.png.source: coloringbook/judge/_jp15rev.mjs FITTED, penny reverse face-review sweep 2026-08-23
penny-rev-1991d.png.reason: ABSENT from _jp1discs.json. This is an addition, not a correction of a published number.

penny-rev-artwork.jpg.via: drawn-rim LINE, inner edge: walk in from 1.15R to the first dark pixel
penny-rev-artwork.jpg.source: coloringbook/judge/_jp15rev.mjs FITTED, penny reverse face-review sweep 2026-08-23

supersedes.why: not a fit: 244 of 720 rays ended at the search-window end. Gasparro's model is a DRAWING on paper, so there is no struck rim for a flood or edge fit to find; the detector locked onto the page.
supersedes.delta: R +44.3%, cy -40.32 px against the drawn-rim fit

penny-rev-artwork.jpg.caveat: This fit locks onto the INNER edge of a hand-drawn line of finite width, so its SCALE carries roughly a percent of bias. Use it for RATIOS (feature height / building height), never for an absolute viewBox number. That caveat is why the entry is usable but not authoritative.

penny-rev.jpg._verdict: NO REPLACEMENT COORDINATE IS PUBLISHED. This entry records the measurement and the refusal.

frozen.via: _rvdisc.fit (rays in 25-155deg dropped before the Kasa solve, which is why this is the LOWEST of the three p95s)

spread.why_it_matters: the two pool-mates agree seven times better under the same three fitters on the same day, so this is the file and not the method

penny-rev.jpg.cause: frame crop, not obliquity. ~11 px of the disc is off the left edge; ~23% of scored rays terminate on the frame at 155-208deg.
penny-rev.jpg.retained_for: T1 (_jt1transfer.mjs POOL_BY_SIDE.reverse.penny). Held-out it sorts penny at 0.517 against 0.193 for the next denomination, and the penny-reverse transfer margin is 0.283 at 38px — both far outside anything a 3.4% registration error moves.
penny-rev.jpg.refused_for: any absolute viewBox coordinate, any band radius, any feature position, any containment number.

unusable.penny-rev-artwork.jpg: the _jp1discs.json entry only — see corrections above for the replacement
unusable.penny-rev.jpg: UNUSABLE FOR GEOMETRY (not for T1 — see _readme). p95 boundary residual 4.90% of R against this project's own 1.0% squareness gate (_jq20indep.mjs:130). The flag text there says 'NOT SQUARE-ON: get a better photograph' and that diagnosis is WRONG: the coin is flat to the sensor. The disc is CROPPED — it runs about 11 px off the left of the 500x500 frame and grazes the bottom, 276 mask pixels sit on the x=0 column, and the residual signature is a straight chord (sector means 150deg +9.9, 180deg -9.4, 210deg +12.6) where an oblique shot gives a smooth two-cycle cosine over all 360deg. WHAT MAKES IT UNUSABLE IS NOT THE RESIDUAL BUT THE DISAGREEMENT: three independent fitters return R 249.28 / 257.74 / 250.89 and cx 238.51 / 224.15 / 234.11 — an 8.46 px spread, 3.39% of R, against 0.47% for BOTH of its pool-mates measured the same way on the same day. A clip-aware refit can be driven under 1.0% but it rests on 165deg of the circle (46%), and the two clip-aware estimators then disagree by 11 px of R. An estimator agreeing with itself is not evidence (COIN-JUDGE 4.1, ledger lesson 15).
